an3.40:1.3: The self as a governing principle, the cosmos as a governing principle, and the Dhamma as a governing principle.
an3.40:1.4: “And what is the self as a governing principle?
an3.40:1.5: There is the case where a monk, having gone to a wilderness, to the foot of a tree, or to an empty dwelling, reflects on this:
an3.40:1.6: ‘It is not for the sake of robes that I have gone forth from the home life into homelessness;
an3.40:1.7: it is not for the sake of almsfood, for the sake of lodgings, or for the sake of this or that state of (future) becoming that I have gone forth from the home life into homelessness.
an3.40:1.8: Simply that I am beset by birth, aging, & death; by sorrows, lamentations, pains, distresses, & despairs; beset by stress, overcome with stress,
an3.40:1.9: (and I hope,) “Perhaps the end of this entire mass of suffering & stress might be known!”
an3.40:1.10: Now, if I were to seek the same sort of sensual pleasures that I abandoned in going forth from home into homelessness—or a worse sort—that would not be fitting for me.’
an3.40:1.12: ‘My persistence will be aroused & not lax; my mindfulness established & not confused; my body calm & not aroused; my mind centered & unified.’
an3.40:1.13: Having made himself his governing principle, he abandons what is unskillful, develops what is skillful, abandons what is blameworthy, develops what is unblameworthy, and looks after himself in a pure way.
an3.40:1.14: This is called the self as a governing principle.
an3.40:2.1: “And what is the cosmos as a governing principle?
an3.40:2.2: There is the case where a monk, having gone to a wilderness, to the foot of a tree, or to an empty dwelling, reflects on this:
an3.40:2.3: ‘It’s not for the sake of robes that I have gone forth from the home life into homelessness;
an3.40:2.4: it’s not for the sake of almsfood, for the sake of lodgings, or for the sake of this or that state of (future) becoming that I have gone forth from the home life into homelessness.
an3.40:2.5: Simply that I am beset by birth, aging, & death; by sorrows, lamentations, pains, distresses, & despairs; beset by stress, overcome with stress,
an3.40:2.6: (and I hope,) “Perhaps the end of this entire mass of suffering & stress might be known!”
an3.40:2.7: Now if I, having gone forth, were to think thoughts of sensuality, thoughts of ill will, or thoughts of harmfulness: Great is the community of this cosmos,
an3.40:2.8: and in the great community of this cosmos there are contemplatives & brahmans endowed with psychic power, clairvoyant, skilled (in reading) the minds of others.
an3.40:2.9: They can see even from afar. Even up close, they are invisible. With their awareness they know the minds of others.
an3.40:2.10: They would know this of me:
an3.40:2.11: “Look, my friends, at this clansman who—though he has in good faith gone forth from the home life into homelessness—remains overcome with evil, unskillful mental qualities.”
an3.40:2.12: There are also devas endowed with psychic power, clairvoyant, skilled (in reading) the minds of others.
an3.40:2.13: They can see even from afar. Even up close, they are invisible. With their awareness they know the minds of others.
an3.40:2.14: They would know this of me:
an3.40:2.15: “Look, my friends, at this clansman who—though he has in good faith gone forth from the home life into homelessness—remains overcome with evil, unskillful mental qualities.”’
an3.40:2.17: ‘My persistence will be aroused & not lax; my mindfulness established & not confused; my body calm & not aroused; my mind centered & unified.’
an3.40:2.18: Having made the cosmos his governing principle, he abandons what is unskillful, develops what is skillful, abandons what is blameworthy, develops what is unblameworthy, and looks after himself in a pure way.
an3.40:2.19: This is called the cosmos as a governing principle.
an3.40:3.1: “And what is the Dhamma as a governing principle?
an3.40:3.2: There is the case where a monk, having gone to a wilderness, to the foot of a tree, or to an empty dwelling, reflects on this:
an3.40:3.3: ‘It’s not for the sake of robes that I have gone forth from the home life into homelessness;
an3.40:3.4: it’s not for the sake of almsfood, for the sake of lodgings, or for the sake of this or that state of (future) becoming that I have gone forth from the home life into homelessness.
an3.40:3.5: Simply that I am beset by birth, aging, & death; by sorrows, lamentations, pains, distresses, & despairs; beset by stress, overcome with stress,
an3.40:3.6: (and I hope,) “Perhaps the end of this entire mass of suffering & stress might be known!”
an3.40:3.7: Now, the Dhamma is well taught by the Blessed One, to be seen here & now, timeless, inviting verification, pertinent, to be experienced by the observant for themselves.
an3.40:3.8: There are companions in the holy life who dwell knowing & seeing it.
an3.40:3.9: If I—having gone forth in this well-taught Dhamma & Vinaya—were to remain lazy & heedless, that would not be fitting for me.’
an3.40:3.11: ‘My persistence will be aroused & not lax; my mindfulness established & not confused; my body calm & not aroused; my mind centered & unified.’
an3.40:3.12: Having made the Dhamma his governing principle, he abandons what is unskillful, develops what is skillful, abandons what is blameworthy, develops what is unblameworthy, and looks after himself in a pure way.
an3.40:3.13: This is called the Dhamma as a governing principle.
an3.40:4.1: There is in the cosmos no secret place
an3.40:4.2: for one who has done an evil deed.
an3.40:4.3: Your own self knows, my good man,
an3.40:4.4: whether you are true or false.
an3.40:5.3: you with evil in yourself that
an3.40:6.2: the fool who goes about off-pitch in the cosmos.
an3.40:6.3: Thus you should go about self-governed, mindful;
an3.40:6.4: governed by the cosmos, masterful, absorbed in jhāna;
an3.40:6.5: governed by the Dhamma, acting in line with the Dhamma.
an3.40:6.6: The sage who makes an effort in truth doesn’t fall back.
an3.40:7.1: Whoever through striving —overpowering Māra, conquering the Ender touches the stopping of birth,
an3.40:7.3: is Such, a knower of the cosmos, wise,
an3.40:7.4: a sage unfashioned with regard to all things.
